subject: Literature in English
examFormat: The syllabus aims to prepare candidates for the UTME by generating, deepening and sustaining interest in literature in English and creating awareness and understanding of the principles and techniques of all genres of literature from diverse cultures. The course objectives are to stimulate and sustain interest in Literature in English; create awareness of the general principles of Literature and the functions of language; appreciate literary works of all genres and across all cultures; and apply knowledge of Literature in English to the understanding of cultural, literary, political and economic activities in society. No exam format or years for the prescribed texts are stated.

topics.name: Drama
objectives: identify the various types of drama
analyse the contents of the various types of drama
compare and contrast the features of different types of drama
demonstrate adequate knowledge of dramatic techniques and stage directions used in each prescribed text
differentiate between styles of selected playwrights
determine the theme of any prescribed text
identify the plot of the play
apply the lessons of the play to social reality
identify the spatial setting and temporal period of the play
topics.content: Types of drama: tragedy, comedy, tragicomedy, melodrama, farce, opera etc. Dramatic techniques: characterisation, dialogue, flashback, mime, costume, music/dance, decor/scenery, acts/scenes, soliloquy/aside, figures of speech. Interpretation of the prescribed texts covers theme, plot, socio-political context and setting.

topics.name: Prose
objectives: differentiate between types of novel
identify the category that each prescribed text belongs to
analyse the components of each type of prose
identify the balance of facts and fiction in literary faction
identify the narrative techniques used in each of the prescribed texts
determine an author's narrative style
distinguish one type of character from another
assess grammar, diction and clarity of expression
determine the thematic preoccupation of the prescribed text
indicate the plot of the novel
identify the setting and period/timing of the novel
relate the prescribed text to social reality
topics.content: Types: prose fiction (novel, novella/novelette, short story); non-fiction (biography, autobiography, memoir); faction (a combination of fact and fiction). Narrative techniques/devices: point of view (omniscient, first person, second person, third person, stream of consciousness, epiphany); characterisation (round, flat, foil, hero, antihero, villain, heroine etc.); language. Textual analysis covers theme, plot, setting (temporal/spatial) and socio-political context.

subtopics.name: So the Path Does not Die (Pede Hollist)
Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured (Susanne Bellefeuille)

topics.name: Poetry
objectives: identify different types of poetry
identify the distinctive features of the poetic types
determine the devices used by various poets
show how poetic devices are used for aesthetic effect in each poem
identify the figure of speech in the texts
show how poetic devices convey message and meaning
deduce the poet's thematic preoccupation from the poem
appraise poetry as an art with moral values
apply the lessons from the poem to social reality
topics.content: Types: sonnet, ode, lyrics, elegy, ballad, panegyric, epic, blank verse etc. Poetic devices: imagery; sound (rhyme/rhythm, repetition, pun, onomatopoeia etc.); diction; persona. Appreciation covers thematic preoccupation, socio-political relevance and style. Prescribed African poems: Once Upon a Time, New Tongue, Night, Not my Business, Hearty Garlands, The Breast of the Sea; non-African: She Walks in Beauty, The Nun's Priest Tale (shortened), The Telephone Call, The Stone.

subtopics.name: The Breast of the Sea (Syl Cheney-Coker)
The Nun's Priest Tale, shortened (Geoffrey Chaucer)

topics.name: General Literary Terms and Principles
objectives: identify literary terms that are specific to drama, prose and poetry
identify areas of overlap in all the genres, e.g. verse in drama and poetry, narration in all the genres
topics.content: Literary terms include foreshadowing, suspense, theatre, monologue, dialogue, soliloquy, symbolism, protagonist, antagonist, figures of speech, satire, stream of consciousness, synecdoche, metonymy etc., in addition to those listed under the different genres.

topics.name: Literary Appreciation
objectives: identify literary devices used in a given passage/extract
provide an interpretation of the given passage/extract
relate the extract to true life experiences
topics.content: Unseen passages/extracts from Drama, Prose and Poetry.
